dedupe_keys.name: once per century geoelectric hazard map and transmission line voltages for the u s high voltage grid lucas et al 2020

description: This resource gives once-per-century geoelectric field estimates at 1,079 magnetotelluric survey sites across the United States and the resulting theoretical voltages on 17,258 high-voltage transmission lines. Greg Lucas, Jeffrey Love, Anna Kelbert, Paul Bedrosian and Joshua Rigler of the USGS built it from 31 years of magnetic field data, selecting 84 geomagnetic storms by Kp and Dst and combining data from 24 observatories with the magnetotelluric sites, as the most complete public hazard analysis for the grid. Once-per-century field strengths span more than three orders of magnitude, from 0.02 V/km at a site in Idaho to 26.8 V/km at a site in Maine. Coverage is the contiguous United States where magnetotelluric data exist. Format and access: maps and tables in an open-access Space Weather article (2020), listed in the USGS Publications Warehouse. Licence: not stated on the page read; free. Caveats: estimates are extrapolated from a few decades of storms and depend on 3-D impedance at survey sites, not on every line route. It supports hazard exposure and resilience analysis of grids against extreme storms. Related catalogue records are the NOAA SWPC geoelectric field models and the USGS Carrington-class geoelectric field estimates.
